# Pick My Secret Santa: full page text

> Complete text of pickmysecretsanta.com's four pages: the homepage (the draw tool and the reveal view), Draw Names Online, Privacy, and Terms.
> Pick My Secret Santa is a free Secret Santa draw tool. Add names and a budget. It draws matches in secret, right in your browser.
> Each person gets a private link with their match, plus six gift ideas inside the budget. A private link is hidden from plain sight, not locked; anyone with a link can open it.
> Gift ideas come from a fixed list of 212 ideas. No ads, no accounts, no store links.
> Text captured from the shipped pages, 2026-10-31.
> Contact: hello@pickmysecretsanta.com

Frequently asked questions
How does this secret santa generator work?
Add every name and pick a budget.
The draw runs in your browser. No one draws their own name.
Each person gets one private link. That link shows just their match.
Do I need an email or an account?
No email or account is needed.
You send each private link yourself.
The site never emails or texts matches.
Can I keep some pairs apart?
Yes, you can mark pairs apart.
Mark pairs who must not draw each other.
The draw keeps marked pairs apart. Too many pairs can block the draw.
Can the organizer see who got whom?
Your screen shows names and links only. It never shows the matches.
Each match lives inside its private link.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. Anyone with a link can open it.
Is this secret santa generator free?
Yes, the full draw is free. There is no sign-up at all.
There are no ads. Each person gets six gift ideas.
Ideas come from 212 real ideas. Every idea fits your budget.
How many people do I need?
You need at least three people. Three is the smallest group that works.
Add a last initial for shared names.
Can I add someone after the draw?
Yes. You have two honest ways.
Draw the whole group again. Add the name first.
Every match is drawn fresh.
Send only the new set of links.
Old links still show the old draw.
Nobody learns a match. The seal stays whole.
Swap in a volunteer. One person gives up their match.
The new person takes that match.
The volunteer buys for the new person.
The old match gets a new Santa.
Three matches change. The group hears nothing.
The price: the volunteer tells you their match.
You set the swap up by hand.
So you learn those matches too.
One corner of the seal is spent.
How do we reveal who had whom?
Pick one swap game before the party.
Try Guess first, Three clues, or Balloon pop. See all eight games in When you swap gifts.
What if I close the tab?
Your links stay saved on this device.
Open this page again to send one.
Nothing is saved on our server.
Clear your saved draw any time.
When you swap gifts
Pick one game for the whole group.
Guess first.
Open one gift at a time, in turns. Each person guesses their Santa first. Only then does the Santa speak up.
Tag clue round.
Write one clue on the gift tag. Read the tag aloud before opening. The group guesses from the clue alone.
Three clues game.
Each Santa gives three clues, one by one. Clues start hard and get easier. The person guesses after each clue.
Note inside the wrap.
Hide a signed note inside the wrapping paper. Your person finds it while they open. Keep the outside of the gift blank.
Stand and point.
After the last gift, all Santas stand up. Each person points at their best guess. Santas sit down when guessed right.
Balloon pop.
Put each Santa name inside a balloon. Each person pops one after opening their gift. The name inside names their Santa.
Video reveal.
Film a short clip before the party. Start in a hat or a mask. Take it off and say your name. Play the clips after the last gift.
All at once.
Tell everyone at once after the last gift. No guessing, no games, all names together. A Santa can stay secret if they want.

Keep it secret.
Want one for your group?
Start your own draw
Free. About 2 minutes.
Give it without giving yourself away
Pick the way that fits your place.
Desk drop.
Leave it on their desk before work starts. Slip away before they sit down. Best when you know their start time.
Doorstep drop.
Set the gift at their front door. Knock once, then walk away fast. Rain coming? Put it under cover first.
Front desk hold.
Leave it with the front desk or mail room. Ask staff to hand it over later. Put only their name on the label.
Helper handoff.
Ask a friend outside the game to deliver it. They say one line only: this is for you. Pick someone who will not spill the name.
Locker stash.
Slip it into their locker, cubby, or drawer. Use a spot they open every day. Make sure no one else can reach it.
Mailbox surprise.
Drop it in their work mailbox slot. Add a tag that says: open later, alone. Small, soft gifts fit this way best.
Plain mail box.
Mail it in a plain, sturdy box. Write no return name or address. Post it early. Holiday mail runs slow.
Clue trail.
Hide the gift somewhere safe nearby. Leave a first clue where they will see it. Each clue leads to the next one. The last clue leads to the gift.
Decoy box.
Put the gift inside a bigger, silly box. Wrap that box in plain paper. The odd shape hides what is inside. Add soft filler so nothing rattles.
Gift table drop.
Put it on the shared gift table early. Arrive before your person does. Then join the crowd like everyone else.
For every way: use plain wrap. Print the tag. Handwriting gives you away.

Pick one game for the whole group.
Guess first.
Open one gift at a time, in turns. Each person guesses their Santa first. Only then does the Santa speak up.

All at once.
Tell everyone at once after the last gift. No guessing, no games, all names together. A Santa can stay secret if they want.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/privacy

Privacy - Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Privacy
The short version:
Names and the draw stay in your browser. Cloudflare Web Analytics counts visits here. PostHog counts draws, shares, and link opens, as counts only. There are no accounts here.
What the draw does
You type names, a budget, and any pairs who should not draw each other.
The draw math runs in your browser.
Nothing you type is sent to us.
Say what a person is into, in your words.
Those words are matched on this device.
They are not sent or saved.
No name is asked for there.
After a draw, your browser saves your links.
They stay on this device only.
That way you can send a link again later.
You can clear them any time with two taps.
On a shared device, clear them when done.
Private links
Each link holds one person's match.
The match sits inside the link itself.
Our server never sees the match.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked.
Anyone with a link can open it.
Send each link only to its person.
You share links with your own apps.
Sharing starts only when you tap a button.
How visits are counted
This site loads Cloudflare Web Analytics.
It sends page and performance counts to Cloudflare.
Cloudflare says its beacon uses no cookies.
This site also loads PostHog.
PostHog counts page views, draws, shares, link opens, and card saves.
Gift idea matches count as a count of picks only.
It also counts return visits.
Start your own draw taps count too.
It counts actions only, never what you type.
No names, matches, gift picks, or link parts are sent.
PostHog sets no cookie on this site.
Your browser keeps one yes-or-no mark on this device.
It says this browser has drawn or peeked before.
It holds no names, matches, gift picks, or links.
It lets a later visit count as a return visit.
Your saved draw stays on this device too.
It holds your names and each person's link.
It is never sent to us or to PostHog.
Counts never include anything inside it.
Children
Adults run the draws on this site.
Some gifts here are for children.
It is not directed at children under 13.
Contact
Questions about privacy: hello@pickmysecretsanta.com.
Changes
Changes will appear on this page.

Terms - Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Terms
These terms cover this website only.
This site is a free Secret Santa tool.
You add names and a budget.
It draws matches and suggests gifts.
There are no ads on this site.
There are no accounts or sign-ups.
The site sells nothing at all.
How the draw works
The draw is random, with two rules.
Nobody draws their own name.
Pairs you mark never draw each other.
The draw runs in your browser.
We never see your group's matches.
Some rule sets cannot form a draw.
The site will say so when that happens.
Where gift ideas come from
Gift ideas come from a fixed list.
The list holds 212 gift ideas.
Your budget is a hard filter.
A gift hint raises matching ideas.
Budget bands are guides, not exact prices.
Stores set real prices, and prices change.
Buying your gift
This site links to no stores.
It takes no payment from you.
It places no orders for you.
You choose where and what to buy.
Check each idea before you buy.
Accounts and data
Names and draws stay in your browser.
Cloudflare Web Analytics counts visits here.
PostHog counts draws, shares, and link opens.
It also counts return visits. All as counts only.
See the
Privacy page
for full details.
No guarantees
This site is provided as is.
We give no warranty of any kind.
We cannot guarantee any gift outcome.
We are not liable for any loss.
Fair use
Use this site only for lawful purposes.
Do not try to break this site.
We may change or stop this site.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/how-does-secret-santa-work

How Does Secret Santa Work? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
How does Secret Santa work?
One gift each. One name each. Nobody knows who has whom until the swap.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
The short version
Secret Santa is a group gift swap with the names hidden.
Agree a budget. One number everyone can afford.
Draw one name each. Your name is the only one you see.
Buy one gift. For your person only, inside the budget.
Swap on the day. Wrapped, labeled with their name, never yours.
That is the whole game. The secret is the fun part.
The rules most groups use
At least three people. Two is just a trade.
No one draws their own name. If it happens, draw again.
One gift, inside the budget. The budget keeps it fair and light.
Label the gift with their name only. Your name stays off it.
Stay secret until the swap. Guessing is half the party.
Run it with this site
The draw runs in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server.
Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
Add every name. Add what each person likes.
Mark pairs to keep apart. Only if some must not draw each other.
Tap Draw the names. Each person gets one private link.
Send each link to its person only. The link shows just their match.
Your screen shows names and links. It never shows the matches.
Each person also gets six gift ideas that fit the budget.
How the online draw works
Ways groups bend it
Keep some pairs apart. Couples and close family often sit the draw out for each other. Mark the pairs before you draw.
Add someone late. Draw the whole group again and the seal stays whole. Or a volunteer gives up their match, and the site names the price out loud: the volunteer tells the organizer their match. Both ways, in full .
White elephant is a cousin, not the same game. There, gifts are swapped and stolen in the open. Secret Santa is one secret match, bought for one person.
Reveal games. End the swap with a guessing game. See all eight reveal games .
Common questions
How many people do we need?
At least three. Three is the smallest group that works.
Can the organizer peek at the matches?
No. The organizer screen shows names and links only.
Each match lives inside its private link.
What budget is normal?
Any one number the whole group can afford.
Most groups land between $10 and $30. Say the number before the draw.
What if someone forgets their person?
Their link still works. Links stay saved on the organizer device too.
The organizer can send the same link again.
Ready when you are
Start your draw

Common questions
What is a good Secret Santa gift under $25?
Match it to what they are into: a small-batch hot sauce trio for the cook, a clip-on book light for the reader. Every idea on this page sits in the under-$25 band of a checked bank of 212 ideas.
Do the gift ideas cost extra?
No. When you run a draw here, each person gets six gift ideas that fit the budget, free. The ideas come from the same bank as this page.
Do you sell these gifts?
No. Ideas are described in plain words, with no store links. Search the name anywhere you like to buy it. Prices move; every idea here sits in the under-$25 band of the bank.
